topics_covered.title: Topic 4.4: HTML Links
short_notes: Hyperlinks connect web pages to other web pages or resources.
The anchor tag <a> is used to create hyperlinks.
The href attribute specifies the destination URL of the link.
Links can open in the same tab or a new tab using target="_blank".
Internal links allow navigation within the same website using element IDs.
key_points: Syntax: Link Text
Absolute URLs point to external websites.
Relative URLs point to files within the same website directory.
topics_covered.explanation: Hyperlinks are the foundation of the World Wide Web, allowing users to navigate seamlessly between documents. The <a> tag wraps around text or images that act as clickable triggers.
topics_covered.diagram_illustration: [User Clicks] ──> About Us ──> Loads about.html in Browser
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: School portals use hyperlinks to connect students from homepages to specific grade-level resource directories.
topics_covered.exam_focus: Distinguishing between absolute paths and relative paths inside the href attribute.

topics_covered.title: Topic 4.5: HTML Tables
short_notes: HTML tables are used to organize data into rows and columns.
The <table> tag defines the table container.
Rows are created using the <tr> tag.
Table headers and data cells are defined using <th> and <td> tags respectively.
Attributes like border, colspan, and rowspan modify table presentation and layout.
key_points: Table hierarchy: <table> -> <tr> -> <th>/<td>
Use of colspan to span cells horizontally across multiple columns.
Use of rowspan to span cells vertically across multiple rows.
topics_covered.explanation: Tables structure tabular data clearly. Headers (<th>) are typically bold and centered by default, while data cells (<td>) contain standard content.
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: School report cards and national examination schedule timetables are frequently formatted using HTML tables on educational websites.
topics_covered.exam_focus: Correct nesting of <tr>, <th>, and <td> elements within a <table> tag.

topics_covered.title: Topic 4.6: HTML Lists
short_notes: HTML provides three main types of lists: Ordered, Unordered, and Description lists.
Ordered lists (<ol>) display items with numbers or letters.
Unordered lists (<ul>) display items with bullet points.
List items in both ordered and unordered lists are defined using the <li> tag.
Lists can be nested inside one another to create multi-level hierarchies.
key_points: Unordered list tag: <ul> with <li> items.
Ordered list tag: <ol> with <li> items.
List type attribute can modify numbering styles (e.g., type="A" or type="i").
topics_covered.explanation: Lists organize items sequentially or categorically. Browsers automatically format bullet points for unordered lists and sequence numbers for ordered lists.

topics_covered.exam_focus: Identifying the correct tags for ordered (<ol>) vs. unordered (<ul>) lists and their item tags (<li>).

topics_covered.title: Topic 4.3: HTML Basics and Document Structure
short_notes: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, used for structuring web pages.
HTML documents must begin with the `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration.

Tags are enclosed in angle brackets, such as `

` for paragraphs and `

` for main headings.

Most HTML elements consist of a starting tag, content, and an ending tag (e.g., `

Hello

`).
The `<head>` section holds metadata, title, and link references, while the `<body>` holds visible elements.
Attributes provide additional information about HTML elements and are specified inside the start tag.
key_points: Case-insensitivity of tags (though lowercase is the modern web standard).
Proper nesting of HTML tags to prevent rendering errors.

The role of empty elements like `
` and `` which do not require closing tags.

topics_covered.title: 5.1 PC Assembly, POST Diagnostics, BIOS/UEFI Configuration, and ESD Safety
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.1 PC Assembly, POST Diagnostics, BIOS/UEFI Configuration, and ESD Safety
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Electrostatic discharge grounding, motherboard form factors, beep codes, thermal paste, and boot order setup.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement & Number Systems: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB). Binary (Base-2), Octal (Base-8), Decimal (Base-10), Hexadecimal (Base-16, digits 0–9 and A–F).

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Digital Ethics, Intellectual Property & E-Waste: Intellectual Property Rights (Copyright protects creative works/code, Patents protect inventions, Trademarks protect brand symbols). Plagiarism vs. Fair Use citation. Digital Divide (gap between technology-rich and technology-poor communities). Green Computing & safe E-Waste recycling of toxic heavy metals (lead, mercury, cadmium).
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
To convert binary 1101₂ to decimal: 1×2³ + 1×2² + 0×2¹ + 1×2⁰ = 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 13₁₀.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
Step 2: To convert binary 1101₂ to decimal: 1×2³ + 1×2² + 0×2¹ + 1×2⁰ = 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 13₁₀.
Step 3: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

book-11-soc-it_ch_5_topic_topic_5_1__har.unit_summary: Study Notes: Topic 5.1: Hardware Troubleshooting. Hardware troubleshooting is the systematic process of identifying, isolating, and rectifying faults in computer physical components.
book-11-soc-it_ch_5_topic_topic_5_1__har.detailed_overview:
Hardware troubleshooting requires a structured, scientific approach. When a computer fails to start, the technician checks the power source, inspects cable connections, and listens to POST beep codes. 

[Diagram: Troubleshooting Flowchart]
[Start: PC Won't Turn On] --> [Check Power Cord & Outlet] --> [Test PSU with Multimeter] --> [Check Motherboard Power Connections] --> [Isolate RAM/CPU if Fans Spin but No Display]

topics_covered.title: Topic 5.1: Hardware Troubleshooting
short_notes: Hardware troubleshooting is the systematic process of identifying, isolating, and rectifying faults in computer physical components.
Common boot failures are often signaled by BIOS/UEFI beep codes or POST (Power-On Self-Test) error messages.
Diagnostic methodology follows a logical sequence: symptom recognition, hypothesis testing, isolation, replacement, and verification.
Power Supply Unit (PSU) failures can prevent systems from powering on completely or cause random reboots.
RAM seating issues frequently trigger blue screens of death (BSOD) or continuous reboot loops.
Thermal throttling and sudden shutdowns are primarily caused by CPU overheating due to dust accumulation or dry thermal paste.
key_points: POST (Power-On Self-Test) checks basic hardware integrity before loading the OS.
Isolation technique involves disconnecting non-essential peripherals to identify short circuits.
Multimeters are utilized to verify correct DC voltage outputs from power supply rails (+5V, +12V, +3.3V).

worked_examples.title: Identifying Power Supply Failure
worked_examples.problem: A school computer fails to show any signs of life (no fan spin, no LED lights) when the power button is pressed. Wall outlet power is verified working.
worked_examples.step_solution: 1. Verify AC power cable integrity. 2. Open the computer case and check ATX power connector seating on the motherboard. 3. Perform a PSU paperclip test to see if the fan spins. 4. Measure rail voltages using a multimeter.
worked_examples.result: Defective Power Supply Unit identified and replaced.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Always discharge capacitors and unplug the PC before opening the case to avoid electrical shock.

book-11-soc-it_ch_5_topic_topic_5_2__bas.unit_summary: Study Notes: Topic 5.2: Basics of Preventive Maintenance. Preventive maintenance consists of regular, planned tasks undertaken to prevent unexpected hardware or software failures.
book-11-soc-it_ch_5_topic_topic_5_2__bas.detailed_overview:
Preventive maintenance is proactive rather than reactive. By maintaining clean ventilation pathways and stable power inputs, hardware components operate within safe thermal and electrical limits. 

| Maintenance Type | Frequency | Action Taken | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Physical Cleaning** | Monthly / Quarterly | Compressed air dusting | Prevent overheating |
| **Electrical Check** | Bi-annually | Inspect AVR and UPS batteries | Protect from surges |
| **Thermal Renewal** | Annually | Reapply thermal paste | Maintain heat transfer |

topics_covered.title: Topic 5.2: Basics of Preventive Maintenance
short_notes: Preventive maintenance consists of regular, planned tasks undertaken to prevent unexpected hardware or software failures.
Physical cleaning involves removing dust from heat sinks, fans, and circuit boards using compressed air and anti-static brushes.
Thermal paste renewal between the CPU and heat sink ensures optimal heat dissipation and prevents thermal shutdown.
Electrical protection devices such as Voltage Regulators (AVR) and Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS) safeguard equipment against power fluctuations.
Software maintenance includes updating device drivers, clearing temporary files, and performing disk defragmentation on HDDs.
key_points: Preventive maintenance reduces Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) by extending hardware lifespan.
Anti-static wrist straps prevent electrostatic discharge (ESD) damage to sensitive microchips.
UPS devices provide battery backup during sudden power interruptions.

Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

Key Takeaway: The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 5.1 Hardware Troubleshooting
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.1 Hardware Troubleshooting
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic 5.1: Hardware Troubleshooting

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Curriculum topic 5.1: Hardware Troubleshooting

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Curriculum topic 5.1: Hardware Troubleshooting

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic 5.1: Hardware Troubleshooting

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

book-11-soc-it_ch_6_topic_types_of_progr.detailed_overview:
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

Key Takeaway: The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Types of Programming Languages
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Types of Programming Languages
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic 6.1: Types of Programming Languages

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic 6.1: Types of Programming Languages

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

topics_covered.topic_title: 1.1 Data, Information, Knowledge, and Wisdom Hierarchy (DIKW)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Transforming raw facts into contextualized information, actionable knowledge, and strategic wisdom.

• Information Systems Pyramid: Data (raw unorganized facts) → Information (processed, contextualized data) → Knowledge (actionable insight) → Wisdom. Organizational IS Hierarchy: 1) Transaction Processing Systems (TPS - daily operational records like POS/ATM); 2) Management Information Systems (MIS - middle-management summary reports); 3) Decision Support Systems (DSS - analytical "what-if" modeling); 4) Executive Information Systems (EIS - strategic dashboards).

• Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning: AI builds intelligent agents capable of perception, reasoning, and decision-making. Subfields: Machine Learning (Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement Learning), Deep Learning (multi-layer neural networks), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision, and Robotics.

Organizational IS Hierarchy: 1) Transaction Processing Systems (TPS - daily operational records like POS/ATM); 2) Management Information Systems (MIS - middle-management summary reports); 3) Decision Support Systems (DSS - analytical "what-if" modeling); 4) Executive Information Systems (EIS - strategic dashboards).

• Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning: AI builds intelligent agents capable of perception, reasoning, and decision-making. • Cloud Computing Service & Deployment Models: Service Models: 1) IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service - virtual servers/storage, e.g. AWS EC2); 2) PaaS (Platform as a Service - runtime & dev tools for developers); 3) SaaS (Software as a Service - ready-to-use browser apps like Google Docs, Office 365). Deployment: Public, Private, Hybrid, Community clouds.

• IoT, Big Data (5 Vs) & E-Government: Internet of Things (IoT) connects smart sensors and actuators over IP networks. Big Data is characterized by the 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. E-Government models: G2C (Government-to-Citizen), G2B (Government-to-Business), G2G (Government-to-Government).
key_points: TPS handles routine daily transactions at the operational level; DSS assists senior managers with unstructured analytical decisions.

book-11-soc-it_ch_1__detailed.detailed_overview:
### 1. Unit Masterclass: Theoretical Foundations & Governing Laws
Unit 1 (Information Systems and Their Applications) is a foundational pillar of the Ethiopian Grade 11 - Social Science Information Technology syllabus. It develops students' analytical rigor, linking fundamental laws and conceptual frameworks to problem-solving strategies and real-world systems.

### 2. Comprehensive Curriculum Breakdown Table
| Section | Topic Title | Core Governing Concept & EUEE Target |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Topic 1** | 1.1 Data, Information, Knowledge, and Wisdom Hierarchy (DIKW) | TPS processes daily transactions while DSS supports complex decisions; Cloud models span I |
| **Topic 2** | 1.2 Components and Types of Information Systems (TPS, MIS, DSS, EIS) | TPS processes daily transactions while DSS supports complex decisions; Cloud models span I |
| **Topic 3** | 1.3 E-Government, E-Commerce, E-Banking (Telebirr/CBE), and E-Learning in Ethiopia | TPS processes daily transactions while DSS supports complex decisions; Cloud models span I |

### 3. Integrated Concept Map & Analytical Intuition
```text
[Unit 1: Information Systems and Their Applications] 
       ├──> Theoretical Principles & Governing Laws
       ├──> Empirical Verification & Analytical Formulas
       └──> Ethiopian Context & Examination Mastery
```

### 4. Real-World Applications Across Ethiopia

Deployment: Public, Private, Hybrid, Community clouds.

• IoT, Big Data (5 Vs) & E-Government: Internet of Things (IoT) connects smart sensors and actuators over IP networks. topics_covered.title: 1.1 Data, Information, Knowledge, and Wisdom Hierarchy (DIKW)
topics_covered.topic_title: 1.1 Data, Information, Knowledge, and Wisdom Hierarchy (DIKW)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Transforming raw facts into contextualized information, actionable knowledge, and strategic wisdom.

• Information Systems Pyramid: Data (raw unorganized facts) → Information (processed, contextualized data) → Knowledge (actionable insight) → Wisdom. Organizational IS Hierarchy: 1) Transaction Processing Systems (TPS - daily operational records like POS/ATM); 2) Management Information Systems (MIS - middle-management summary reports); 3) Decision Support Systems (DSS - analytical "what-if" modeling); 4) Executive Information Systems (EIS - strategic dashboards).

• Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning: AI builds intelligent agents capable of perception, reasoning, and decision-making. Subfields: Machine Learning (Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement Learning), Deep Learning (multi-layer neural networks), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision, and Robotics.

• Cloud Computing Service & Deployment Models: Service Models: 1) IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service - virtual servers/storage, e.g. AWS EC2); 2) PaaS (Platform as a Service - runtime & dev tools for developers); 3) SaaS (Software as a Service - ready-to-use browser apps like Google Docs, Office 365). Deployment: Public, Private, Hybrid, Community clouds.

• IoT, Big Data (5 Vs) & E-Government: Internet of Things (IoT) connects smart sensors and actuators over IP networks. Big Data is characterized by the 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. E-Government models: G2C (Government-to-Citizen), G2B (Government-to-Business), G2G (Government-to-Government).
key_points: TPS handles routine daily transactions at the operational level; DSS assists senior managers with unstructured analytical decisions.
SaaS provides complete end-user software over the internet, whereas IaaS provides raw virtualized hardware infrastructure.
The 5 Vs of Big Data are Volume (scale), Velocity (speed), Variety (formats), Veracity (trustworthiness), and Value (utility).

topics_covered.title: 1.2 Components and Types of Information Systems (TPS, MIS, DSS, EIS)
topics_covered.topic_title: 1.2 Components and Types of Information Systems (TPS, MIS, DSS, EIS)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Hardware, software, data, procedures, and people; operational vs tactical vs strategic enterprise systems.

• Information Systems Pyramid: Data (raw unorganized facts) → Information (processed, contextualized data) → Knowledge (actionable insight) → Wisdom. Organizational IS Hierarchy: 1) Transaction Processing Systems (TPS - daily operational records like POS/ATM); 2) Management Information Systems (MIS - middle-management summary reports); 3) Decision Support Systems (DSS - analytical "what-if" modeling); 4) Executive Information Systems (EIS - strategic dashboards).

• Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning: AI builds intelligent agents capable of perception, reasoning, and decision-making. Subfields: Machine Learning (Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement Learning), Deep Learning (multi-layer neural networks), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision, and Robotics.

• Cloud Computing Service & Deployment Models: Service Models: 1) IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service - virtual servers/storage, e.g. AWS EC2); 2) PaaS (Platform as a Service - runtime & dev tools for developers); 3) SaaS (Software as a Service - ready-to-use browser apps like Google Docs, Office 365). Deployment: Public, Private, Hybrid, Community clouds.

• IoT, Big Data (5 Vs) & E-Government: Internet of Things (IoT) connects smart sensors and actuators over IP networks. Big Data is characterized by the 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. E-Government models: G2C (Government-to-Citizen), G2B (Government-to-Business), G2G (Government-to-Government).
key_points: TPS handles routine daily transactions at the operational level; DSS assists senior managers with unstructured analytical decisions.
SaaS provides complete end-user software over the internet, whereas IaaS provides raw virtualized hardware infrastructure.
The 5 Vs of Big Data are Volume (scale), Velocity (speed), Variety (formats), Veracity (trustworthiness), and Value (utility).

topics_covered.title: 1.2 Components and Types of Information Systems (TPS, MIS, DSS, EIS)
topics_covered.topic_title: 1.2 Components and Types of Information Systems (TPS, MIS, DSS, EIS)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Hardware, software, data, procedures, and people; operational vs tactical vs strategic enterprise systems.

• Information Systems Pyramid: Data (raw unorganized facts) → Information (processed, contextualized data) → Knowledge (actionable insight) → Wisdom. Organizational IS Hierarchy: 1) Transaction Processing Systems (TPS - daily operational records like POS/ATM); 2) Management Information Systems (MIS - middle-management summary reports); 3) Decision Support Systems (DSS - analytical "what-if" modeling); 4) Executive Information Systems (EIS - strategic dashboards).

• Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning: AI builds intelligent agents capable of perception, reasoning, and decision-making. Subfields: Machine Learning (Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement Learning), Deep Learning (multi-layer neural networks), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision, and Robotics.

• Cloud Computing Service & Deployment Models: Service Models: 1) IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service - virtual servers/storage, e.g. AWS EC2); 2) PaaS (Platform as a Service - runtime & dev tools for developers); 3) SaaS (Software as a Service - ready-to-use browser apps like Google Docs, Office 365). Deployment: Public, Private, Hybrid, Community clouds.

• IoT, Big Data (5 Vs) & E-Government: Internet of Things (IoT) connects smart sensors and actuators over IP networks. Big Data is characterized by the 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. E-Government models: G2C (Government-to-Citizen), G2B (Government-to-Business), G2G (Government-to-Government).
key_points: TPS handles routine daily transactions at the operational level; DSS assists senior managers with unstructured analytical decisions.
SaaS provides complete end-user software over the internet, whereas IaaS provides raw virtualized hardware infrastructure.
The 5 Vs of Big Data are Volume (scale), Velocity (speed), Variety (formats), Veracity (trustworthiness), and Value (utility).

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Modern Information Systems integrate organizational transaction workflows with emerging cloud, AI, and IoT architectures to automate public services, banking, and enterprise analytics.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Digital public service portals, B2B/B2C/G2C models, mobile money architecture, and national digital transformation.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: TPS handles routine daily transactions at the operational level; DSS assists senior managers with unstructured analytical decisions.
- **Key Principle**: SaaS provides complete end-user software over the internet, whereas IaaS provides raw virtualized hardware infrastructure.
- **Key Principle**: The 5 Vs of Big Data are Volume (scale), Velocity (speed), Variety (formats), Veracity (trustworthiness), and Value (utility).

**Visual / Experimental Schema:**

| **Governing Law** | TPS processes daily transactions while DSS supports complex decisions; Cloud mod... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | Very high frequency in EUEE: matching IS types (TPS, MIS, DSS) to management lev... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Fayda National Digital ID, e-Visa portal (G2C), electronic single-window customs (G2B), and Telebirr/CBE Birr mobile fintech exemplify national digital transformation.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Very high frequency in EUEE: matching IS types (TPS, MIS, DSS) to management levels, distinguishing IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS, and identifying the 5 Vs of Big Data.

TPS processes daily transactions while DSS supports complex decisions; Cloud models span IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning; neural networks, computer vision, and Amharic/local NLP.

• Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning: AI builds intelligent agents capable of perception, reasoning, and decision-making. • Cloud Computing Service & Deployment Models: Service Models: 1) IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service - virtual servers/storage, e.g. AWS EC2); 2) PaaS (Platform as a Service - runtime & dev tools for developers); 3) SaaS (Software as a Service - ready-to-use browser apps like Google Docs, Office 365). Deployment: Public, Private, Hybrid, Community clouds.

• IoT, Big Data (5 Vs) & E-Government: Internet of Things (IoT) connects smart sensors and actuators over IP networks. Big Data is characterized by the 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. E-Government models: G2C (Government-to-Citizen), G2B (Government-to-Business), G2G (Government-to-Government).

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Modern Information Systems integrate organizational transaction workflows with emerging cloud, AI, and IoT architectures to automate public services, banking, and enterprise analytics.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning; neural networks, computer vision, and Amharic/local NLP.

- **Key Principle**: TPS handles routine daily transactions at the operational level; DSS assists senior managers with unstructured analytical decisions.
- **Key Principle**: SaaS provides complete end-user software over the internet, whereas IaaS provides raw virtualized hardware infrastructure.
- **Key Principle**: The 5 Vs of Big Data are Volume (scale), Velocity (speed), Variety (formats), Veracity (trustworthiness), and Value (utility).

**Visual / Experimental Schema:**

| **Examination Traps** | Very high frequency in EUEE: matching IS types (TPS, MIS, DSS) to management lev... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

Ethiopia's Fayda National Digital ID, e-Visa portal (G2C), electronic single-window customs (G2B), and Telebirr/CBE Birr mobile fintech exemplify national digital transformation.

Very high frequency in EUEE: matching IS types (TPS, MIS, DSS) to management levels, distinguishing IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS, and identifying the 5 Vs of Big Data.

TPS processes daily transactions while DSS supports complex decisions; Cloud models span IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Relational Database Model, Schemas, Keys, and Integrity Constraints
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.1 Relational Database Model, Schemas, Keys, and Integrity Constraints
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Relations, tuples, attributes, primary/foreign/candidate/composite keys, entity integrity, and referential integrity.

• Relational Database Fundamentals (RDBMS): Organizes data into 2D relations (Tables) consisting of Tuples (Rows/Records) and Attributes (Columns/Fields). Advantages over flat files: eliminates data redundancy, enforces data integrity, supports concurrent multi-user access, and provides centralized security.

• Keys & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling: Primary Key (PK): uniquely identifies each row and CANNOT be NULL. Foreign Key (FK): attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table to enforce Referential Integrity. ER Diagram symbols: Rectangle = Entity, Ellipse = Attribute (underlined = PK), Diamond = Relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N). Note: M:N relationships are resolved using a junction/associative table.

• Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF): Process of structuring tables to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies: 1) First Normal Form (1NF): Atomic values only (no repeating groups or multi-valued attributes); 2) Second Normal Form (2NF): In 1NF + no Partial Dependency (non-key attributes depend on the whole composite PK); 3) Third Normal Form (3NF): In 2NF + no Transitive Dependency (non-key attributes depend ONLY on the PK, never on another non-key attribute).

• Structured Query Language (SQL): 1) DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP; 2) DML (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT INTO, UPDATE ... SET, DELETE FROM; 3) DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MAX(), MIN().
key_points: A Primary Key must be unique and NOT NULL; a Foreign Key can contain duplicate values or NULLs (unless restricted) and links child records to a parent Primary Key.
Memory trick for Normalization: "The key (1NF), the whole key (2NF), and nothing but the key (3NF)!"
In SQL, the WHERE clause filters individual rows BEFORE grouping, whereas the HAVING clause filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY clause.

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Cardinality ratios (1:1, 1:M, M:N), eliminating repeating groups, partial dependencies, and transitive dependencies.

• Relational Database Fundamentals (RDBMS): Organizes data into 2D relations (Tables) consisting of Tuples (Rows/Records) and Attributes (Columns/Fields). Advantages over flat files: eliminates data redundancy, enforces data integrity, supports concurrent multi-user access, and provides centralized security.

• Keys & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling: Primary Key (PK): uniquely identifies each row and CANNOT be NULL. Foreign Key (FK): attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table to enforce Referential Integrity. ER Diagram symbols: Rectangle = Entity, Ellipse = Attribute (underlined = PK), Diamond = Relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N). Note: M:N relationships are resolved using a junction/associative table.

• Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF): Process of structuring tables to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies: 1) First Normal Form (1NF): Atomic values only (no repeating groups or multi-valued attributes); 2) Second Normal Form (2NF): In 1NF + no Partial Dependency (non-key attributes depend on the whole composite PK); 3) Third Normal Form (3NF): In 2NF + no Transitive Dependency (non-key attributes depend ONLY on the PK, never on another non-key attribute).

• Structured Query Language (SQL): 1) DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP; 2) DML (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT INTO, UPDATE ... SET, DELETE FROM; 3) DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MAX(), MIN().

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Relations, tuples, attributes, primary/foreign/candidate/composite keys, entity integrity, and referential integrity.

• Relational Database Fundamentals (RDBMS): Organizes data into 2D relations (Tables) consisting of Tuples (Rows/Records) and Attributes (Columns/Fields). Advantages over flat files: eliminates data redundancy, enforces data integrity, supports concurrent multi-user access, and provides centralized security.

• Keys & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling: Primary Key (PK): uniquely identifies each row and CANNOT be NULL. Foreign Key (FK): attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table to enforce Referential Integrity. ER Diagram symbols: Rectangle = Entity, Ellipse = Attribute (underlined = PK), Diamond = Relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N). Note: M:N relationships are resolved using a junction/associative table.

• Structured Query Language (SQL): 1) DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP; 2) DML (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT INTO, UPDATE ... SET, DELETE FROM; 3) DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MAX(), MIN().

worked_example.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization
worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_example.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

worked_example.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization
worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_example.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

worked_example.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization
worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_example.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

book-11-soc-it_ch_3_topic_sql_ddl_and_dm.detailed_overview:
Database Management Systems (DBMS) provide the persistent data backbone of all software applications. ER modeling, 3NF normalization, and SQL queries guarantee fast, consistent, and anomaly-free data storage.

Key Takeaway: PK uniquely identifies records while FK links tables; 1NF requires atomicity, 2NF removes partial dependency, 3NF removes transitive dependency.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: National student examination registries at EAES, commercial banking ledgers, and hospital electronic medical record systems in Ethiopia rely on normalized relational SQL databases.

topics_covered.topic_title: 3.3 SQL DDL and DML Queries (CREATE, ALTER, SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Creating relational tables with constraints, filtering with WHERE/ORDER BY, aggregate functions, and inner joins.

• Relational Database Fundamentals (RDBMS): Organizes data into 2D relations (Tables) consisting of Tuples (Rows/Records) and Attributes (Columns/Fields). Advantages over flat files: eliminates data redundancy, enforces data integrity, supports concurrent multi-user access, and provides centralized security.

• Keys & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling: Primary Key (PK): uniquely identifies each row and CANNOT be NULL. Foreign Key (FK): attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table to enforce Referential Integrity. ER Diagram symbols: Rectangle = Entity, Ellipse = Attribute (underlined = PK), Diamond = Relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N). Note: M:N relationships are resolved using a junction/associative table.

• Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF): Process of structuring tables to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies: 1) First Normal Form (1NF): Atomic values only (no repeating groups or multi-valued attributes); 2) Second Normal Form (2NF): In 1NF + no Partial Dependency (non-key attributes depend on the whole composite PK); 3) Third Normal Form (3NF): In 2NF + no Transitive Dependency (non-key attributes depend ONLY on the PK, never on another non-key attribute).

• Structured Query Language (SQL): 1) DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP; 2) DML (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT INTO, UPDATE ... SET, DELETE FROM; 3) DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MAX(), MIN().
key_points: A Primary Key must be unique and NOT NULL; a Foreign Key can contain duplicate values or NULLs (unless restricted) and links child records to a parent Primary Key.
Memory trick for Normalization: "The key (1NF), the whole key (2NF), and nothing but the key (3NF)!"
In SQL, the WHERE clause filters individual rows BEFORE grouping, whereas the HAVING clause filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY clause.

worked_example.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization
worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_example.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

quiz_item.question: A table is in Second Normal Form (2NF), but contains an attribute "DepartmentLocation" that depends on "DepartmentID" (a non-key attribute) rather than directly on the Primary Key "EmployeeID". Which normal form is violated?
options: Third Normal Form (3NF) due to Transitive Dependency
First Normal Form (1NF) due to Non-Atomic Values
Second Normal Form (2NF) due to Partial Dependency
Referential Integrity due to a missing Foreign Key
quiz_item.explanation: When a non-key attribute (DepartmentLocation) depends on another non-key attribute (DepartmentID) instead of directly on the Primary Key, it is a Transitive Dependency, which violates Third Normal Form (3NF).

worked_example.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization
worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_example.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

topics_covered.topic_title: 4.1 Website Planning, UI/UX Wireframing, and HTML5 Semantic Architecture
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Site maps, accessibility standards, semantic tags, multimedia embedding, and structured HTML5 forms.

• OSI 7-Layer Model & TCP/IP Suite: OSI Layers (Bottom to Top — "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away"): 1) Physical (bits, cables, hubs), 2) Data Link (frames, MAC addresses, switches), 3) Network (packets, IP addresses, routers), 4) Transport (segments, TCP reliable vs UDP fast port delivery), 5) Session, 6) Presentation (encryption, compression), 7) Application (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, DNS, DHCP).

• Transmission Media & Network Topologies: Guided wired media: Twisted Pair (UTP/STP with RJ-45 connector), Coaxial, Fiber-Optic cable (transmits light pulses via total internal reflection; immune to EMI, highest bandwidth). Topologies: Star (all nodes connect to central switch; easy troubleshooting), Bus, Ring, Mesh (highest fault tolerance: n(n-1)/2 cables).

• IPv4 Addressing, Subnetting & Core Services: IPv4 is a 32-bit address written as 4 dotted decimal octets (e.g., 192.168.1.10); IPv6 is 128-bit hexadecimal. Class C default subnet mask is 255.255.255.0 (/24), yielding 2⁸ - 2 = 254 usable host addresses. DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses; DNS translates domain names (moe.gov.et) to IP addresses; NAT maps private IPs to a public IP.

• Cybersecurity & CIA Triad: Confidentiality (encryption: Symmetric AES vs. Asymmetric RSA public/private key), Integrity (hashing: SHA-256), Availability (redundancy, DDoS mitigation). Threats: Virus (attaches to host file), Worm (self-replicates across network without user action), Trojan (disguised as legitimate software), Ransomware, Phishing, SQL Injection.
key_points: Switches operate at Layer 2 (Data Link) using physical MAC addresses; Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network) using logical IP addresses.
For a subnet with h host bits, the number of usable host IP addresses is ALWAYS 2^h - 2 (subtracting 1 for the Network ID and 1 for the Broadcast address).
Fiber-optic cables transmit data as light pulses and are completely immune to electromagnetic interference (EMI).

topics_covered.topic_title: 4.2 Advanced CSS3 Layouts (Box Model, Flexbox, Grid, Media Queries)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Specificity cascade, responsive breakpoints, flexible box alignment, and two-dimensional grid templates.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).
key_points: In CSS, an #id selector has higher specificity than a .class selector, which has higher specificity than a tag selector.
In Python, range(1, 6) generates [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] — the stop value (6) is strictly EXCLUDED!
Lists in Python are mutable (can be modified after creation), whereas Tuples and Strings are immutable.

topics_covered.title: 4.3 JavaScript Programming: Variables, Functions, DOM Events, and Form Validation
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.3 JavaScript Programming: Variables, Functions, DOM Events, and Form Validation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Document Object Model selection, event listeners, client-side input validation, and dynamic UI updates.

• Relational Database Fundamentals (RDBMS): Organizes data into 2D relations (Tables) consisting of Tuples (Rows/Records) and Attributes (Columns/Fields). Advantages over flat files: eliminates data redundancy, enforces data integrity, supports concurrent multi-user access, and provides centralized security.

• Keys & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling: Primary Key (PK): uniquely identifies each row and CANNOT be NULL. Foreign Key (FK): attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table to enforce Referential Integrity. ER Diagram symbols: Rectangle = Entity, Ellipse = Attribute (underlined = PK), Diamond = Relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N). Note: M:N relationships are resolved using a junction/associative table.

• Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF): Process of structuring tables to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies: 1) First Normal Form (1NF): Atomic values only (no repeating groups or multi-valued attributes); 2) Second Normal Form (2NF): In 1NF + no Partial Dependency (non-key attributes depend on the whole composite PK); 3) Third Normal Form (3NF): In 2NF + no Transitive Dependency (non-key attributes depend ONLY on the PK, never on another non-key attribute).

• Structured Query Language (SQL): 1) DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP; 2) DML (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT INTO, UPDATE ... SET, DELETE FROM; 3) DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MAX(), MIN().
key_points: A Primary Key must be unique and NOT NULL; a Foreign Key can contain duplicate values or NULLs (unless restricted) and links child records to a parent Primary Key.
Memory trick for Normalization: "The key (1NF), the whole key (2NF), and nothing but the key (3NF)!"
In SQL, the WHERE clause filters individual rows BEFORE grouping, whereas the HAVING clause filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY clause.

worked_example.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization
worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_example.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

quiz_item.question: A table is in Second Normal Form (2NF), but contains an attribute "DepartmentLocation" that depends on "DepartmentID" (a non-key attribute) rather than directly on the Primary Key "EmployeeID". Which normal form is violated?
options: Third Normal Form (3NF) due to Transitive Dependency
First Normal Form (1NF) due to Non-Atomic Values
Second Normal Form (2NF) due to Partial Dependency
Referential Integrity due to a missing Foreign Key
quiz_item.explanation: When a non-key attribute (DepartmentLocation) depends on another non-key attribute (DepartmentID) instead of directly on the Primary Key, it is a Transitive Dependency, which violates Third Normal Form (3NF).

worked_examples.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization (4.3 JavaScript Programming: Variables, Functions, DOM Events, and Form Validation)
worked_examples.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_examples.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_examples.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

topics_covered.topic_title: 4.1 Website Planning, UI/UX Wireframing, and HTML5 Semantic Architecture
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Site maps, accessibility standards, semantic tags, multimedia embedding, and structured HTML5 forms.

• OSI 7-Layer Model & TCP/IP Suite: OSI Layers (Bottom to Top — "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away"): 1) Physical (bits, cables, hubs), 2) Data Link (frames, MAC addresses, switches), 3) Network (packets, IP addresses, routers), 4) Transport (segments, TCP reliable vs UDP fast port delivery), 5) Session, 6) Presentation (encryption, compression), 7) Application (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, DNS, DHCP).

• Transmission Media & Network Topologies: Guided wired media: Twisted Pair (UTP/STP with RJ-45 connector), Coaxial, Fiber-Optic cable (transmits light pulses via total internal reflection; immune to EMI, highest bandwidth). Topologies: Star (all nodes connect to central switch; easy troubleshooting), Bus, Ring, Mesh (highest fault tolerance: n(n-1)/2 cables).

• IPv4 Addressing, Subnetting & Core Services: IPv4 is a 32-bit address written as 4 dotted decimal octets (e.g., 192.168.1.10); IPv6 is 128-bit hexadecimal. Class C default subnet mask is 255.255.255.0 (/24), yielding 2⁸ - 2 = 254 usable host addresses. DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses; DNS translates domain names (moe.gov.et) to IP addresses; NAT maps private IPs to a public IP.

• Cybersecurity & CIA Triad: Confidentiality (encryption: Symmetric AES vs. Asymmetric RSA public/private key), Integrity (hashing: SHA-256), Availability (redundancy, DDoS mitigation). Threats: Virus (attaches to host file), Worm (self-replicates across network without user action), Trojan (disguised as legitimate software), Ransomware, Phishing, SQL Injection.

Fiber-optic cables transmit data as light pulses and are completely immune to electromagnetic interference (EMI).

topics_covered.topic_title: 4.2 Advanced CSS3 Layouts (Box Model, Flexbox, Grid, Media Queries)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Specificity cascade, responsive breakpoints, flexible box alignment, and two-dimensional grid templates.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).

In Python, range(1, 6) generates [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] — the stop value (6) is strictly EXCLUDED!
Lists in Python are mutable (can be modified after creation), whereas Tuples and Strings are immutable.

topics_covered.topic_title: 4.3 JavaScript Programming: Variables, Functions, DOM Events, and Form Validation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Document Object Model selection, event listeners, client-side input validation, and dynamic UI updates.

• Relational Database Fundamentals (RDBMS): Organizes data into 2D relations (Tables) consisting of Tuples (Rows/Records) and Attributes (Columns/Fields). Advantages over flat files: eliminates data redundancy, enforces data integrity, supports concurrent multi-user access, and provides centralized security.

• Keys & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling: Primary Key (PK): uniquely identifies each row and CANNOT be NULL. Foreign Key (FK): attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table to enforce Referential Integrity. ER Diagram symbols: Rectangle = Entity, Ellipse = Attribute (underlined = PK), Diamond = Relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N). Note: M:N relationships are resolved using a junction/associative table.

• Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF): Process of structuring tables to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies: 1) First Normal Form (1NF): Atomic values only (no repeating groups or multi-valued attributes); 2) Second Normal Form (2NF): In 1NF + no Partial Dependency (non-key attributes depend on the whole composite PK); 3) Third Normal Form (3NF): In 2NF + no Transitive Dependency (non-key attributes depend ONLY on the PK, never on another non-key attribute).

• Structured Query Language (SQL): 1) DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP; 2) DML (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT INTO, UPDATE ... SET, DELETE FROM; 3) DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MAX(), MIN().
key_points: A Primary Key must be unique and NOT NULL; a Foreign Key can contain duplicate values or NULLs (unless restricted) and links child records to a parent Primary Key.
Memory trick for Normalization: "The key (1NF), the whole key (2NF), and nothing but the key (3NF)!"
In SQL, the WHERE clause filters individual rows BEFORE grouping, whereas the HAVING clause filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY clause.

topics_covered.topic_title: 4.1 Website Planning, UI/UX Wireframing, and HTML5 Semantic Architecture
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Site maps, accessibility standards, semantic tags, multimedia embedding, and structured HTML5 forms.

• OSI 7-Layer Model & TCP/IP Suite: OSI Layers (Bottom to Top — "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away"): 1) Physical (bits, cables, hubs), 2) Data Link (frames, MAC addresses, switches), 3) Network (packets, IP addresses, routers), 4) Transport (segments, TCP reliable vs UDP fast port delivery), 5) Session, 6) Presentation (encryption, compression), 7) Application (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, DNS, DHCP).

• Transmission Media & Network Topologies: Guided wired media: Twisted Pair (UTP/STP with RJ-45 connector), Coaxial, Fiber-Optic cable (transmits light pulses via total internal reflection; immune to EMI, highest bandwidth). Topologies: Star (all nodes connect to central switch; easy troubleshooting), Bus, Ring, Mesh (highest fault tolerance: n(n-1)/2 cables).

• IPv4 Addressing, Subnetting & Core Services: IPv4 is a 32-bit address written as 4 dotted decimal octets (e.g., 192.168.1.10); IPv6 is 128-bit hexadecimal. Class C default subnet mask is 255.255.255.0 (/24), yielding 2⁸ - 2 = 254 usable host addresses. DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses; DNS translates domain names (moe.gov.et) to IP addresses; NAT maps private IPs to a public IP.

• Cybersecurity & CIA Triad: Confidentiality (encryption: Symmetric AES vs. Asymmetric RSA public/private key), Integrity (hashing: SHA-256), Availability (redundancy, DDoS mitigation). Threats: Virus (attaches to host file), Worm (self-replicates across network without user action), Trojan (disguised as legitimate software), Ransomware, Phishing, SQL Injection.

- **Key Principle**: Switches operate at Layer 2 (Data Link) using physical MAC addresses; Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network) using logical IP addresses.

core_formulas_rules.explanation: OSI 7-Layer Model & TCP/IP Suite: OSI Layers (Bottom to Top — "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away"): 1) Physical (bits, cables, hubs), 2) Data Link (frames, MAC addresses, switches), 3) Network (packets, IP addresses, routers), 4) Transport (segments, TCP reliable vs UDP fast port delivery), 5) Session, 6) Presentation (encryption, compression), 7) Application (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, DNS, DHCP).
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications apply.

core_formulas_rules.explanation: Transmission Media & Network Topologies: Guided wired media: Twisted Pair (UTP/STP with RJ-45 connector), Coaxial, Fiber-Optic cable (transmits light pulses via total internal reflection; immune to EMI, highest bandwidth). Topologies: Star (all nodes connect to central switch; easy troubleshooting), Bus, Ring, Mesh (highest fault tolerance: n(n-1)/2 cables).
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications apply.

core_formulas_rules.explanation: IPv4 Addressing, Subnetting & Core Services: IPv4 is a 32-bit address written as 4 dotted decimal octets (e.g., 192.168.1.10); IPv6 is 128-bit hexadecimal. Class C default subnet mask is 255.255.255.0 (/24), yielding 2⁸ - 2 = 254 usable host addresses. DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses; DNS translates domain names (moe.gov.et) to IP addresses; NAT maps private IPs to a public IP.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications apply.

topics_covered.topic_title: 4.2 Advanced CSS3 Layouts (Box Model, Flexbox, Grid, Media Queries)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Specificity cascade, responsive breakpoints, flexible box alignment, and two-dimensional grid templates.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).
key_points: In CSS, an #id selector has higher specificity than a .class selector, which has higher specificity than a tag selector.
In Python, range(1, 6) generates [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] — the stop value (6) is strictly EXCLUDED!
Lists in Python are mutable (can be modified after creation), whereas Tuples and Strings are immutable.

• Relational Database Fundamentals (RDBMS): Organizes data into 2D relations (Tables) consisting of Tuples (Rows/Records) and Attributes (Columns/Fields). Advantages over flat files: eliminates data redundancy, enforces data integrity, supports concurrent multi-user access, and provides centralized security.

• Keys & Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling: Primary Key (PK): uniquely identifies each row and CANNOT be NULL. Foreign Key (FK): attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table to enforce Referential Integrity. ER Diagram symbols: Rectangle = Entity, Ellipse = Attribute (underlined = PK), Diamond = Relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:N). Note: M:N relationships are resolved using a junction/associative table.

• Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF): Process of structuring tables to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies: 1) First Normal Form (1NF): Atomic values only (no repeating groups or multi-valued attributes); 2) Second Normal Form (2NF): In 1NF + no Partial Dependency (non-key attributes depend on the whole composite PK); 3) Third Normal Form (3NF): In 2NF + no Transitive Dependency (non-key attributes depend ONLY on the PK, never on another non-key attribute).

• Structured Query Language (SQL): 1) DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE TABLE, ALTER, DROP; 2) DML (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT INTO, UPDATE ... SET, DELETE FROM; 3) DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MAX(), MIN().
key_points: A Primary Key must be unique and NOT NULL; a Foreign Key can contain duplicate values or NULLs (unless restricted) and links child records to a parent Primary Key.
Memory trick for Normalization: "The key (1NF), the whole key (2NF), and nothing but the key (3NF)!"
In SQL, the WHERE clause filters individual rows BEFORE grouping, whereas the HAVING clause filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY clause.

worked_example.title: Worked Problem: SQL Query Construction & Normalization
worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.
worked_example.step_solution:
1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score
2. Specify source table: FROM Students
3. Apply row conditions using AND: WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85
4. Sort descending by Score: ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.result: SELECT FullName, Score FROM Students WHERE Grade = 12 AND Region = 'Addis Ababa' AND Score >= 85 ORDER BY Score DESC;
worked_example.examiner_note: Remember: ASC sorts lowest-to-highest (default), whereas DESC sorts highest-to-lowest!

worked_example.problem: Given a table Students(StudentID, FullName, Grade, Region, Score), write an SQL query to retrieve the FullName and Score of all Grade 12 students from "Addis Ababa" who scored at least 85, sorted from highest to lowest score.

1. Specify columns to retrieve: SELECT FullName, Score

topics_covered.topic_title: 5.1 PC Assembly, POST Diagnostics, BIOS/UEFI Configuration, and ESD Safety
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Electrostatic discharge grounding, motherboard form factors, beep codes, thermal paste, and boot order setup.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). - **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).

- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary/hexadecimal to decimal numbers, distinguishi... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; binary base-2 powers digital logic; ethical IT requires respecting copyright and safe e-waste disposal.

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Python Data Structures: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, and String Manipulation
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Python Data Structures: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, and String Manipulation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Zero-based indexing, slicing, mutable lists vs immutable tuples, key-value dictionaries, and string methods.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).
key_points: In CSS, an #id selector has higher specificity than a .class selector, which has higher specificity than a tag selector.
In Python, range(1, 6) generates [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] — the stop value (6) is strictly EXCLUDED!
Lists in Python are mutable (can be modified after creation), whereas Tuples and Strings are immutable.

topics_covered.topic_title: 6.2 Modular Functions, Scope, File Input/Output, and Exception Handling
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Defining reusable functions, local vs global scope, reading/writing text and CSV files, and try-except blocks.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).

topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Python Data Structures: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, and String Manipulation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Zero-based indexing, slicing, mutable lists vs immutable tuples, key-value dictionaries, and string methods.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).

topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Python Data Structures: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, and String Manipulation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Zero-based indexing, slicing, mutable lists vs immutable tuples, key-value dictionaries, and string methods.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Defining reusable functions, local vs global scope, reading/writing text and CSV files, and try-except blocks.

• Web Authoring (HTML5, CSS3 & JavaScript DOM): HTML5 defines semantic structure (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <footer>, <form>, <table>). CSS3 controls presentation via the Box Model (Content → Padding → Border → Margin), selectors (element, .class, #id), and responsive Flexbox/Grid layouts. JavaScript adds client-side interactivity via DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, addEventListener).

• Algorithms, Flowcharts & Control Structures: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Flowchart symbols: Oval = Start/End, Parallelogram = Input/Output, Rectangle = Process, Diamond = Decision (if/else branch). Time complexity: O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear, O(n²) bubble sort.

• Python Programming & Data Structures: Python uses indentation for code blocks. Control flow: if / elif / else, for i in range(n), while condition. Data structures: List [mutable, ordered, 0-indexed], Tuple (immutable, ordered), Set {unique elements}, Dictionary {key: value pairs}. Functions defined with def name(params): return value.

• Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Data Formats: Four Pillars of OOP: 1) Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding private state); 2) Inheritance (child class reuses parent class attributes/methods); 3) Polymorphism (method overriding/same interface for different types); 4) Abstraction. Data interchange: JSON (lightweight key-value syntax) vs. XML (custom tags).

Lists in Python are mutable (can be modified after creation), whereas Tuples and Strings are immutable.
